correctness.rationale: The real smooth ell_3^2 Birkhoff criterion x1|x1|y1+x2|x2|y2=0 reduces all unit orthogonal pairs, modulo signed-coordinate isometries and tangent orientation, to x=(t,1)/(1+t^3)^(1/3), y=±(1,-t²)/(1+t⁶)^(1/3), t>=1, together with axis pairs of value 1. After signed scaled lambda s the cubed ratio is F(t,s)=[1+t³+|s|³(1+t⁶)]/[|t+s|³+|1-s t²|³]. Independent exact expansion verifies all three eliminated sign-region denominators-minus-numerator: for 0<=s<=t^-2, s²t[3(t³+1)-2s t^5]>0; for -t<=s<=0, v=-s, v²(3t^4+3t-2v)>0; for s<=-t, v=-s, t[3v²(t³-1)+6tv-2t²]>0. On s>=t^-2, u=t³>=1, h=s t²>=1 gives exact R(u,h)=[u²(1+u)+h³(1+u²)]/[(u+h)³+u²(h-1)³]. Both finite boundary values are <1 and the explicit difference D-N=-u[3h²(u-1)-6hu+2u] proves R->1 on every unbounded path, by cases h bounded, u>=h³, and u<h³ with h->infinity. R(16,5)=36477/25645>1, so an interior maximizer exists. Independently derived both derivative numerator polynomials and exact resultant factor 4u^13(u+1)^4 Q(u)P(u), with Q>0; exact Sturm root count gives exactly one u>=1 root of degree-ten P, isolated (16.1428,16.1429). Independently checked the linear subresultant 4A(u)h-B(u) modulo P, rational interval positivity A>0,B-16A>0,20A-B>0 and derivative divisibility after h=B/(4A). The unique admissible stationary point is the global maximum, rho=1.4225104283683517897..., mu3=rho^(1/3)=1.124652845212756113... . Finite numerical checks were not used for the universal result.

The 2021 primary paper defines precisely mu_p and proves only broad estimates; Theorem 5.6 gives mu_3(ell_3)<=3^(1/3), a nonsharp upper bound. The strongest published exact same-invariant neighbor covers p=4, and the same-space classical mu_1(ell_3^2), T_perp and isosceles findings use different functionals; the L4 generalized mu2 theorem has different exponent and a quartic moment envelope. No reported table or stronger arbitrary-exponent classification covers the degree-ten cubic target. value.rationale: The Gastinel–Joly generalized rectangular constant is a standard, geometrically motivated invariant of Birkhoff–James orthogonality. The real cubic Banach plane is the first non-Hilbert smooth odd-integer exponent and a natural exact benchmark, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The full cubic exact value is not implied by published p=3 classical mu1, p=4 generalized mu4, nor the nonsharp general estimates. Its extremizer is genuinely interior and unique modulo natural sign/permutation normalizations, requiring a substantive semialgebraic global certificate (factorized resultant, Sturm count, subresultant, escape control). A future geometric-constant researcher could use this exact planar value and tangent orbit for quantitative comparisons and benchmarks, despite its narrow two-dimensional scope. A paper-sized general theorem is not required.
risks: No general p or arbitrary dimension classification is claimed.
The answer has a degree-ten algebraic representation rather than simple radicals; this does not diminish its exact invariant status.
